grammar_contract.input: A parse-that state over a JavaScript string at a valid UTF-16 parser offset; the observation door starts at offset 0.
grammar_contract.operation: Inspect at most the next three positions and return whether they would start a CSS number: sign then digit; sign then dot then digit; dot then digit; or digit.
grammar_contract.consumption: Always zero UTF-16 code units. The parser always succeeds with boolean true/false, leaves the offset unchanged, and emits no diagnostics.
grammar_contract.preprocessing: The positive alphabet is only ASCII +, -, ., and digits. CSS preprocessing changes no positive case; any NUL, newline variant, surrogate, or non-ASCII code point is an anything-else case. Reading UTF-16 code units is therefore boolean-equivalent for this operation while offsets remain source-native.
grammar_contract.diagnostics: Always readonly []; false is the normative predicate result, not a parse error.
grammar_contract.recovery: Not applicable; the operation consumes nothing and cannot fail.
grammar_contract.serialization: Not applicable; the result is a predicate boolean.
grammar_contract.no_throw: For every string input, return exactly one boolean with no diagnostic and no exception.
grammar_contract.work_bound: O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space after input existence; inspect no more than three UTF-16 code units and allocate no token, CST, substring, or intermediate array.

benchmark.statistics: Report raw nanoseconds, median, MAD, and geometric mean of paired time ratios. Strict win requires the upper endpoint of a one-sided 95% percentile bootstrap interval over paired log-ratios, 10000 resamples with the fixed schedule seed, to be below 0 (ratio below 1.0).
